day_shape: State Department unveils fresh Iran shadow-oil sanctions (1 individual, 16 entities, 8 vessels), reported US-Iran MoU draft awaits Trump and Mojtaba Khamenei approval, IDF intensifies Lebanon offensive striking Beirut and Qaraoun Dam, and explosions reported near Strait of Hormuz/Bandar Abbas.

threads.label: State Dept sanctions Iran shadow oil economy
threads.summary: The State Department announced coordinated sanctions targeting Iran's illicit oil revenue, designating one individual, 16 entities and identifying eight vessels involved in petroleum transport. Defa Press confirmed Treasury's OFAC listing, framing it as continued US maximum pressure.

threads.label: US-Iran MoU draft awaits approvals
threads.summary: Reports said US and Iranian negotiators agreed a memorandum of understanding extending the ceasefire, pending sign-off from Trump and Mojtaba Khamenei. The White House confirmed the draft, while Vance said Washington is "not there yet" with Tehran but close.

threads.label: Strait of Hormuz incidents and denials
threads.summary: Iranian state media reported explosions near the Strait of Hormuz and Bandar Abbas, with Defa Press claiming Iranian forces fired missiles from southern Iran toward unspecified targets and IRIB claiming a US aircraft was downed near Bushehr. CENTCOM rejected the downing claim, stating all US air assets are accounted for, and Times of Israel noted a greater proportion of non-Iranian ships transiting Hormuz.

threads.label: IDF Lebanon offensive intensifies
threads.summary: The IDF struck Beirut for the first time in three weeks, issued evacuation orders for Tyre and Ain Qana, and disclosed strikes on Hezbollah operatives near the Qaraoun Dam. Spokesman Defrin said nearly a third of Hezbollah's pre-2023 force has been killed or wounded, with 2,500 fighters lost since March, while Iran's foreign ministry condemned the attacks.

threads.label: Gaza operations expand beyond truce terms
threads.summary: Netanyahu told the Jordan Valley Conference that Israel controls over half of Gaza and ordered the IDF to seize 70% of the Strip, beyond ceasefire terms. The IDF confirmed killing Hamas Gaza City Brigade deputy commander Imad Aslim and said Hamas is operating fiber-optic drones modelled on Hezbollah's.

threads.label: Regional alignments and Iran-linked plots
threads.summary: New Iraqi PM Ali al-Zaidi urged armed groups to operate under state institutions, a Kata'ib Hezbollah commander was indicted on eight charges over attempted attacks on Jewish targets, and the Jerusalem Post reported an Iran intelligence-linked hacker group breached LA transit systems stealing 700GB. Analysis pieces flagged US-Oman strain after Trump's Gulf-waters warning and Saudi distrust of US protection.

threads.label: Khamenei office Majlis message cycle
threads.summary: Khamenei's office released and amplified a written message from Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei marking the anniversary of the Majlis, calling for focus on the "resistance economy" slogan and post-war reconstruction from the second and third imposed wars. Defa Press circulated media reactions and Pezeshkian posted on cooperation with Malaysia and Pakistan over ceasefire mediation.

threads.label: Humanitarian reporting and TPS extension
threads.summary: UN OCHA and WHO issued updates on the Middle East escalation, noting fragile ceasefires and persistent health threats particularly in Lebanon. The US Homeland Security Department automatically extended Lebanon's Temporary Protected Status designation through 27 November 2026.

The deputy commander of Hamas's Gaza City Brigade was killed in an Israeli airstrike in the Gaza Strip this week, the IDF confirms.

Imad Aslim was killed in a strike on Wednesday, and a funeral was held for him in Gaza City on Thursday.

The IDF says Aslim was the deputy commander of the Gaza City Brigade and also the commander of the brigade's Zeitoun Battalion.

Aslim commanded the battalion during the October 7 onslaught, when its terrorists invaded Israel, and recently, he worked to advance attacks on troops, "and therefore he was an immediate threat," the military says.

events.title: Extension of Lebanon Designation for Temporary Protected Status
events.summary: The designation of Lebanon for Temporary Protected Status (TPS), which was set to expire on May 27, 2026, is automatically extended to November 27, 2026. Under the TPS statute, if the Secretary does not determine whether a foreign state continues to meet the conditions for designation for TPS at least 60 days before the expiration of the country's current TPS designation, the period of designation is automatically extended for six months. Rapidly unfolding events in Lebanon in March 2026 impacted the Department's ability to conduct a thorough review of prevailing country conditions for the Secretary's timely consideration and determination.

events.title: Over 135 Hezbollah targets were struck over the past day, the military says. In southern Lebanon and the eastern Beqaa Valley, the IDF says that it struck 10 rocket launching sites, along with a Hezbollah training camp. In Tyre, 15 Hezbollah infrastructure sites used to advance attacks were struck, according to the military. The Israeli Air Force also struck and killed several Hezbollah operatives who were seen leaving a rocket-launching site used in an attack on troops, the IDF adds.
